solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Uncompromising doctor offered less breadth (5)

indicatorNotes.less: less means minus, so B for breadth comes out of BID

blocks.note: to doctor results is to rig them
offered = BID, minus B for breadth

annotation.surface: A stubborn doctor who stints on how broad his offer is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' wants to be DR or MO; here it is the verb, to tamper with.
annotation.definitionFit: A rigid position is one that will not bend, which is to say uncompromising.

entries.clue: Beating player, down the first large glass (6)

indicatorNotes.down the first: to be down something is to have lost it, so the player loses his first letter

blocks.note: a beating player is a DRUMMER, which loses its first letter D

annotation.surface: A drummer drinking, having sunk the first of several.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'down the first' as drinking the first glass; it is the drummer who is down his first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, if a rare word: the rummer is a big stemmed goblet, once used for toasts.

entries.clue: Armies’ legions marshalled — by him? (13)

indicatorNotes.marshalled: to marshal troops is to arrange them in order, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Who drew up all these armies and legions in their ranks?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the description: a generalissimo is exactly the man by whom armies are marshalled.
annotation.definitionFit: A generalissimo is a supreme commander of several armies combined.

entries.clue: Writer fed up with novel every so often (5)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read upwards, so FED turns round
indicatorNotes.every so often: taking a letter every so often means every other one

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of nOvEl

annotation.surface: An author who has had enough of his novel now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as bored, but in a down clue it asks for FED written bottom to top.
annotation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the writer of Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders.

entries.clue: Putting wrong weapon in to load warplane (10)

indicatorNotes.to load: loading a plane means putting cargo inside it, so SWORD and IN go into MIG

blocks.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet

annotation.surface: An armourer fitting the wrong weapon to a fighter jet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting' is a phrasing, not placing: putting something wrong means wording it badly. 'In' is part of the cargo, not a container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Miswording something is putting it wrongly, in the sense of expressing it badly.

entries.clue: Tommy’s dish of eggs, nearly half flipped (4,3)

indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly means not quite complete, so SEMI loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.flipped: flipped over, the whole string reads backwards

blocks.note: nits are the eggs of lice
half = SEMI, nearly all of it

annotation.surface: A soldier's plate of eggs, half of them turned over.
annotation.walkthrough: Tommy is the traditional name for a British private soldier. 'Half' is not an instruction to halve anything: it is SEMI.
annotation.definitionFit: A mess tin is the metal dish a soldier eats from in the field.

entries.clue: British grandmaster replaced missing pieces (5-7)

blocks.note: Nigel Short is an English chess grandmaster

annotation.surface: A chess report: the British grandmaster swapped the pieces he had lost.
annotation.walkthrough: Chess makes 'pieces' look like the men on the board; they are coins, and you are short of some.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone short-changed has been given too little change, so is missing some pieces of money.

entries.clue: Sets of balls have scattered on top (8)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls

annotation.surface: Somebody has sets of balls strewn about.
annotation.walkthrough: An over is the cricket unit of six deliveries from one bowler.
annotation.definitionFit: Seed oversown is scattered over ground that is already sown.

entries.clue: Trail parent in unwavering line (5)

blocks.note: to dog someone is to trail them

annotation.surface: Following a parent who walks a perfectly straight line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line' is a party line, a doctrine held to, not something walked.
annotation.definitionFit: Dogma is a doctrine laid down and held to without deviation.

entries.clue: Part of UK tending to tweet idiocies (10)

blocks.note: twittery = given to twittering, as a bird tweets

annotation.surface: A region of the UK whose people are always posting silly things online.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' suggests social media, but TWITTERY is the old bird's chatter.
annotation.definitionFit: Nitwittery is the behaviour of nitwits: foolishness, idiocies.
annotation.definitionNote: 'idiocies' is plural, the answer a mass noun covering them

entries.clue: Small number with dog left time to get home (6)

indicatorNotes.left: the dog sits on the left, so CUR is written before FEW

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: A handful of people with a dog, leaving in time to be home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed; it is the position, putting CUR to the left of FEW.
annotation.definitionFit: A curfew is the time by which people must be indoors.

entries.clue: Practical article you abridged to do with stretching (7)

indicatorNotes.abridged: an abridged text is cut short, so TENSILE loses its last letter

blocks.note: U = you, as in text messages
TENSILE, relating to tension, cut short

annotation.surface: A handy item that you can cut down to size if it stretches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abridged' sits after 'you' but works on the word that follows.
annotation.definitionFit: A utensil is a practical implement, especially one for the kitchen.

entries.clue: Force retreat across English lines without structure (4,5)

indicatorNotes.across: REVERSE lies across the E, so the E goes inside it

annotation.surface: An army pulls back over English lines that have no fortifications.
annotation.walkthrough: The military picture makes 'lines' trenches; they are lines of poetry.
annotation.definitionFit: Free verse is poetry without regular metre or rhyme, lines without formal structure.

entries.clue: Father of 30 healthy sons? (5)

annotation.surface: A father with thirty strapping boys.
annotation.walkthrough: 30 is the cross-reference to 30 across, SCI-FI; H. G. Wells is often called its father.
annotation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells, author of The Time Machine, is known as a father of science fiction.
annotation.definitionNote: 'sons' gives only S; the plural is surface

entries.clue: Sailor washed up mug, one Connor uses at sea (8,6)

indicatorNotes.at sea: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to mug someone is to rob them

annotation.surface: A sailor Connor keeps a mug on board and it ends up on a beach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Washed up' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: Crusoe was a sailor cast ashore by a shipwreck.
annotation.definitionFit: Defoe's Robinson Crusoe is the archetypal shipwrecked sailor, washed up on a desert island.

entries.clue: Aims often in this when running? (9)

annotation.definition: Aims often in this when running?

indicatorNotes.running: running as in a liquid running, so the letters flow into a new order

annotation.surface: A candidate's aims are often set out in a document when running for office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Running' does two jobs: it stirs the letters, and it is running for election, when parties publish their aims.
annotation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published statement of a party's aims, issued when it stands for election.

entries.clue: Scottish steps eroded, several concrete reportedly (9,4)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, not seen, so ATE and REAL are taken by their sound

blocks.note: eroded = ate (away), which sounds like EIGHT
concrete = real, which sounds like REEL

annotation.surface: A report on steps worn away and several made of concrete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steps' sound like a staircase; they are dance steps. 'Concrete' is the adjective, meaning real.
annotation.definitionFit: The eightsome reel is a Scottish country dance for eight people.

entries.clue: Serious art making money? (7)

blocks.note: 'art' is the old verb, as in 'thou art', so this is old English for 'you are earning'

annotation.surface: A question of whether serious art can pay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Art' is not painting: it is the old verb, as in 'thou art', and 'thou earnest' says the same as 'thou art earning'.
annotation.definitionFit: An earnest person is serious and sincere in intent.

entries.clue: Name in opera, one gathers (9)

indicatorNotes.gathers: to gather is to take in, so TOSCA plus I takes N IN inside

annotation.surface: Somebody hears of a name in the opera world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One gathers' looks like 'I hear', a throwaway aside; it is a real instruction, and the name in opera is a conductor, not a singer.
annotation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini, the Italian conductor, was one of the great names in opera.

entries.clue: Small group of birds keeps out of harm’s way (5)

blocks.note: Aves is the zoological class of birds

annotation.surface: A little flock of birds stays safely away from danger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Group' wants to be a flock; it is the scientific class, Aves.
annotation.definitionFit: To save someone is to keep them out of harm's way.

entries.clue: Foul was Peter Shilton wasting time at the end — hardly a penalty (4,2,3,5)

indicatorNotes.Foul: a foul mess is a disordered one, so the letters are scrambled
indicatorNotes.wasting: wasting something is losing it, so the E goes from the fodder

blocks.note: the last letter of timE, which is removed

annotation.surface: A goalkeeper commits a foul by time-wasting late on and barely gets punished.
annotation.walkthrough: Peter Shilton was England's long-serving goalkeeper, and time-wasting is a football offence. 'Time at the end' is not T: it is the last letter of 'time'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase describes a punishment so mild it barely counts, playing on 'penalty' in the football surface.

entries.clue: Suspect character back in Soho Square between pub and empty shops (9)

indicatorNotes.back in: the back of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.between: the letters sit between PH and SS

blocks.note: nine is a square number, three times three

annotation.surface: A dodgy figure seen at the rear of a Soho square, somewhere between the pub and the boarded-up shops.
annotation.walkthrough: Soho Square is a real London square, which glues the two words together; they must be split.
annotation.definitionFit: Phoniness is a fake, suspect character, the quality of being phoney.

entries.clue: Unusual tidiness maintained (8)

indicatorNotes.Unusual: unusual means not in its usual form, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A rare state of tidiness that was kept up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maintained' looks like 'kept up', agreeing with tidiness; it means asserted.
annotation.definitionFit: To maintain that something is so is to insist on it.

entries.clue: Extravagant display of euphorbia around lake (7)

indicatorNotes.around: around means encircling, so the plant grows round the lake and SPURGE takes L inside

blocks.note: spurge is the common name for euphorbia

annotation.surface: A lavish planting of euphorbia round a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: Euphorbia is the botanical name; the setter wants its common name, spurge.
annotation.definitionFit: A splurge is a showy outburst of extravagance.

entries.clue: Man in field almost cutting from side to side (5,5)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word, so EXTRACT loses its last letter

blocks.note: a cutting from a paper is an EXTRACT, less its last letter
over = across, from one side to the other

annotation.surface: A farmhand in a field, mowing it almost from one side to the other.
annotation.walkthrough: Extra cover is a fielding position in cricket, on the off side between cover and mid-off.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in cricket, fielding positions are named for the player who stands there, so extra cover is one fielder.

entries.clue: Old man breaking lock and turning over residence? (10)

annotation.definition: Old man breaking lock and turning over residence?

indicatorNotes.breaking: PA breaks into TRESS, splitting it

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair
one's old man is one's father, PA
RES = residence, as in des res

annotation.surface: An old codger forcing a lock and ransacking a house.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a housebreaker as well as building the word, which is why it ends in a question mark: a trespasser need not be a burglar.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks a lock and turns over a house has certainly entered without permission.

entries.clue: Defendant unhappy with right to make fresh start (10)

indicatorNotes.to make fresh start: R takes the place of the first letter, giving the word a new start

blocks.note: R = right; it replaces the D

annotation.surface: A defendant in low spirits who has the right to begin again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fresh start' is the instruction: DESPONDENT keeps everything but its first letter, which becomes R.
annotation.definitionFit: In some cases, divorce and appeals especially, the defendant is called the respondent.

entries.clue: Opposition speaker was up and down California during election (6,8)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read upwards, so LIVED turns round

annotation.surface: An opposition politician who campaigned in California, sometimes high and sometimes low.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up and down' reads as a pair, but they split: 'up' turns LIVED over and 'down' is simply SAD.
annotation.definitionFit: A devil's advocate argues the opposing side for the sake of argument.

entries.clue: Guys test compass when cycling, becoming separated (12)

indicatorNotes.when cycling: cycling moves letters round from front to back, so MENT goes to the end

annotation.surface: Some men testing a compass on a bike ride lose track of one another.
annotation.walkthrough: MENTESTRANGE is built first, then its first four letters cycle to the back.
annotation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the process of people becoming separated from one another.

entries.clue: America’s far right? (4,5)

blocks.note: the country itself, not its voters
the surface wants extreme right-wing politics; the setter means the right-hand edge of a map

annotation.surface: A question about America's extreme right-wing politics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Far right' reads as politics, but it is geography: with north at the top, the right-hand edge of America is the east coast.
annotation.definitionFit: On a map, the east coast is as far right as the United States goes.

entries.clue: Not straying at uni, say (2,6)

blocks.note: keeping to the set route, as a ship or a plan does
a student at university is on a course

annotation.surface: A student who keeps to the straight and narrow at university.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the second definition as one example of being on a course.
annotation.definitionFit: Something on course is keeping to its intended route, not straying.

entries.clue: Speculative works kept back by prolific songwriter (3-2)

indicatorNotes.kept: the letters are kept inside the words
indicatorNotes.back: back means in the reverse direction, so the hidden letters read right to left

blocks.note: prolIFIC Songwriter, read right to left

annotation.surface: An unreleased collection held back by a prolific songwriter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speculative works' sounds like investments; it is fiction that speculates about the future.
annotation.definitionFit: Science fiction is speculative fiction, imagining what might be.

entries.clue: Some on the Danube swimming even in case of sewage (8)

indicatorNotes.swimming: swimming things move about, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.case of: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Some people go swimming in the Danube even when sewage is in it.
annotation.walkthrough: Vienna stands on the Danube, so some of the people on it are Viennese.
annotation.definitionFit: The Viennese live in Vienna, a city on the Danube.

entries.clue: Angry spot in your ear swells in two directions (5,3)

indicatorNotes.in your ear: what goes in your ear is heard, so SEE is taken for its sound

annotation.surface: An inflamed spot in the ear swelling in two directions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Angry spot' and 'swells' paint a boil; the swells are waves and the spot is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A cross sea has waves running from two directions at once.

entries.clue: Well-painted room is covered with new cheap tiles, unfortunately (7,6)

indicatorNotes.unfortunately: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A nicely decorated room ruined by a floor of new cheap tiles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well-painted' is an understatement: Michelangelo painted its ceiling.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sistine Chapel in the Vatican is famous for Michelangelo's frescoes.

entries.clue: Winning big game, European getting off on it? (7,5)

blocks.note: to land a prize is to win it
a stag is a big-game animal

annotation.surface: A European getting a thrill out of winning a big match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting off on it' reads as slang for enjoying something; it is literal, stepping off a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A landing stage is a platform where passengers get off boats.

entries.clue: First smell meat left on bar uncovered (5,3)

indicatorNotes.on: on means placed after, so smell, meat and left follow the A from bar

blocks.note: bAr with its outer letters removed

annotation.surface: A cook first sniffs the meat left out on the counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the smell, meat and left after the A of 'bar', which reads first.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'first' as a sentence adverb, as in 'first, be kind', and 'above all' play the same role of putting one thing ahead.

entries.clue: Feet ahead, rowing crew wait to hear (8)

indicatorNotes.to hear: both pieces are taken by their sound

blocks.note: a four is a rowing boat with its crew of four

annotation.surface: Oars forward, a rowing crew waits to listen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feet ahead' reads like a rowing order; together the words mean the front feet.
annotation.definitionFit: Forepaws are an animal's front feet, the ones ahead.

entries.clue: Great Lakes’ fish company stores can be found west of Chicago (5)

indicatorNotes.stores: CO stores the letters inside itself
indicatorNotes.west of: west is the left of a map, so IS goes to the left of the C of Chicago

blocks.note: to be found = to be, IS

annotation.surface: A fish company whose shops are all out west.
annotation.walkthrough: The cisco is a North American whitefish, a Great Lakes species. Cisco is also a Californian company, which the surface plays on.
annotation.definitionFit: The cisco, or lake herring, is a whitefish of the Great Lakes.

entries.clue: Another nearby horse shot behind screens upset me (10)

indicatorNotes.screens: to screen is to hide behind, so LATE holds EM inside
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns ME upside down

blocks.note: a shot at something is a stab

annotation.surface: Someone upset by a horse shot behind the screens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'horse' suggest a vet's grim duty, but a shot is a try, a stab.
annotation.definitionFit: A stablemate is another horse kept in the same stable.

entries.clue: Good time is something to consider, opine hosts (12)

indicatorNotes.hosts: a host holds guests, so SAY holds the rest inside

blocks.note: a factor is something to take into account

annotation.surface: Someone opining that a good time is worth weighing up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good time' is not a party: 'Good' is the definition and 'time' is T.
annotation.definitionFit: A school-report sense: 'good' as a grade of adequate, which is what satisfactory marks.
annotation.definitionNote: 'Good' in the sense of acceptable, adequate

entries.clue: Issue lifting large part of church using widely-spaced frames (4-5)

indicatorNotes.lifting: in a down clue, lifting means raising, so EMIT reads upwards

blocks.note: to issue = to EMIT, reading upwards
the apse is the rounded end of a church

annotation.surface: A fund-raising issue: lifting the big end of a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lifting' only applies to the first word, which is why it sits between 'Issue' and 'large'.
annotation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography takes frames at long intervals and plays them back fast.

entries.clue: Read an outrageous column which boosts circulation (10)

indicatorNotes.outrageous: outrageous means wildly out of order, so READ AN is rearranged

blocks.note: a column of troops is a line

annotation.surface: A shocking newspaper column that increases a paper's sales.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circulation' reads as newspaper sales, but it is the blood.
annotation.definitionFit: Adrenaline raises the heart rate and so boosts the circulation of the blood.
annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing in for the noun

entries.clue: Old vases with a record player on shelves (8)

annotation.surface: Antique vases and a gramophone on the shelves.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means stacked above. 'Shelves' is the verb, to put off, not a place for vases.
annotation.definitionFit: To adjourn a matter is to shelve it for later.

entries.clue: Piece coming through from an overanxious Russian oligarch (7)

indicatorNotes.Piece coming through from: a piece of the following words carries the answer

annotation.surface: A report from a nervy Russian tycoon.
annotation.walkthrough: The hidden letters start in 'from', a word that reads as part of the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Vladimir Romanov is a Russian-born businessman who owned Heart of Midlothian football club.

entries.clue: Brief memo set up fundraising programme, saving hours (7)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word reads upwards
indicatorNotes.saving: saving means except, so H for hours is left out

blocks.note: a TELETHON less H for hours

annotation.surface: A quick note about a charity broadcast, organised to save time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saving' sounds like rescue, but it means 'except'.
annotation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for short messages.

entries.clue: Living on notice in guesthouse without qualification (5,3,6)

indicatorNotes.in: RE AD go in the guesthouse, B AND B

annotation.surface: Staying at a guesthouse under notice to leave, with no qualifications.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Living' is a noun here, as in earning a living.
annotation.definitionFit: Your bread and butter is your basic livelihood, what you live on.

entries.clue: Bishop using speech about saint in school for detention (7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means surrounding, so the speech wraps round the saint and ORAL takes ST inside

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam

annotation.surface: A bishop giving a talk about a saint in a school detention.
annotation.walkthrough: A borstal was a British institution for young offenders, replaced in 1982.
annotation.definitionFit: Borstals were schools where young offenders were detained.

entries.clue: Period certainly finishing fine and free (6)

indicatorNotes.finishing: AY comes at the finish of the word

annotation.surface: A time that is certainly ending, fine and free.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Period' is loose on purpose: a day is a period of time.
annotation.definitionFit: Friday is a day, a period of twenty-four hours.

entries.clue: Reduced drug dose returned to trial (5)

indicatorNotes.Reduced: reduced means made smaller, so PILL loses a letter
indicatorNotes.returned: to return is to go back the way you came, so TO is written from its end

blocks.note: a PILL is a dose of a drug, shortened

annotation.surface: A cut drug dose goes back into testing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link word before the definition, but it is part of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as a noun: a pilot is a small-scale test run before a full launch, as with a TV pilot.

entries.clue: Upright walls I take for granted (5)

indicatorNotes.walls: to wall something is to enclose it, so POST goes round I

annotation.surface: An honest person says: I take it for granted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Walls' is a verb here, enclosing I.
annotation.definitionFit: To posit something is to assume it as a basis for argument.

entries.clue: Easily convinced doctor sure could! (9)

indicatorNotes.doctor: to doctor something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A gullible patient says the doctor sure could.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is not a physician this time but the verb that stirs the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Credulous people believe things too readily.

entries.clue: Show the people we are nearly arrived (5)

indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly all of HERE, so it loses its last letter

blocks.note: we are here = we have arrived; nearly gives HER

annotation.surface: Put on a show, people: we have almost got here.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' is a verb: to show someone to their seat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: an usher's job is showing people to their seats.

entries.clue: Farmer hurried fruit on trees, losing half (7)

indicatorNotes.losing half: the second half of the word falls away

blocks.note: CHERRIES grow on trees; the first four of eight letters

annotation.surface: A grower rushing to his orchard, half the crop gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On trees' only narrows the fruit down to CHERRIES.
annotation.definitionFit: A rancher farms cattle on a ranch.

entries.clue: Bridge player that was inaccurate with hearts, holding king (5)

indicatorNotes.holding: holding means grasping inside, so NOT keeps the king, R, in its hand

blocks.note: the jokey tag 'Not!' takes back what was just said

annotation.surface: A bridge player who misplayed his hearts while holding the king.
annotation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, so North is one of them.
annotation.definitionFit: North is one of the four seats at a bridge table.

entries.clue: Class temp with flex emptied the pine dresser, finally (6,7)

indicatorNotes.emptied: emptied of its middle, THE leaves TE

blocks.note: supply is an old adverb meaning supplely, with flexibility
to pine for is to ache for

annotation.surface: A temp arrives with an electric cable and clears out the pine dresser.
annotation.walkthrough: A supply teacher is the British name for a substitute teacher. 'Pine' is a verb, to long for.
annotation.definitionFit: A supply teacher covers a class temporarily when the regular teacher is away.

entries.clue: Articulate animal? Trained parrot, d’oh (9)

indicatorNotes.Trained: training reshapes something, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A talking animal: a trained parrot saying 'D'oh'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' reads as well-spoken, as a talking parrot would be, but it means jointed.
annotation.definitionFit: Arthropods, such as insects and crabs, have jointed, articulated legs.

entries.clue: Women’s shelter keeps male chromosome score (6)

indicatorNotes.keeps: a shelter keeps people in, so TENT holds W inside, with Y kept on the end

blocks.note: the Y chromosome is the male one

annotation.surface: A refuge for women that takes in a man as well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Score' is a number: twenty.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from counting: a score is a set of twenty, as in 'three score years and ten'.

entries.clue: Film director’s knowledge and short career prove marketable (3,7)

indicatorNotes.short: short means cut, so RUSH loses its last letter

blocks.note: ken = knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'
to career is to RUSH, cut short
a product that proves marketable sells

annotation.surface: A film director's know-how and brief career turn out to be a selling point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Career' is a verb, to rush headlong.
annotation.definitionFit: Ken Russell was a British film director of Women in Love and Tommy.

entries.clue: Like a riddle, say, heard in its entirety (5)

indicatorNotes.say, heard: say and heard both point to sound

annotation.surface: Answering a riddle requires hearing it right through.
annotation.walkthrough: A riddle is a coarse sieve, so 'riddle' is not a puzzle here.
annotation.definitionFit: A riddle, the sieve, is full of holes, so it is holey.
